title: dynamic-range-limit interplay
blurb: Applies CSS dynamic-range-limit values (no-limit, constrained, standard, and dynamic-range-limit-mix) to paired 'standard' and 'extended' canvases and reads computed values live.
question: Can CSS dynamic-range-limit dynamically cap an 'extended' 2D canvas down to SDR headroom without recreating the canvas context?
result: In Chrome 153 headless, CSS.supports('dynamic-range-limit', ...) returns true and getComputedStyle echoes all four values including dynamic-range-limit-mix(standard 50%, no-limit 50%); visual HDR capping requires an HDR display and Chrome 160+ reflecting extended mode.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 headless (SDR display); HDR visual capping not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: Because toneMapping is immutable after context creation, toggling HDR headroom on hover or focus requires pairing Canvas2D with CSS dynamic-range-limit
friction.repro: Create a 2D canvas with toneMapping: { mode: 'standard' }; it cannot later opt into extended headroom without recreating the context and redrawing.
friction.workaround: Create the canvas once with toneMapping: { mode: 'extended' } and apply CSS dynamic-range-limit: standard on thumbnails and no-limit on focused viewers.
